title: Pre-budget meeting: bridge and capital tender awards
subtitle: Also covered: fees increase, OLG funding policy, vehicle pre-approval, Elora Community Centre renovation, East Mill Street and Beatty Line.
overview: Council held its first 2023 budget meeting, which combined education on the budget with five early project approvals. Staff presented pressures including inflation, low assessment growth, insurance costs and Bill 23. A draft capital budget was reviewed but not decided; final budget discussion is planned for February.

Council awarded tenders for two West Garafraxa bridge replacements (24-WG and 16-WG), the East Mill Street reconstruction in Elora and the Elora Community Centre renovation. It also pre-approved the Beatty Line reconstruction in Fergus. Staff said tendering in the fall produced more bids and better pricing than the cancelled spring 2022 tender. Mayor Watters stepped out for the 16-WG item because of a declared conflict of interest.

On policy, Council approved the 2023 fees and charges by-law, an amended OLG funding allocation policy that adds dedicated Community Impact and Heritage categories, and advance approval of vehicle purchases for 2023 and 2024. Residents will see work on roads, bridges and streetscapes start in 2023, and the Elora arena is expected to reopen in January 2024.

decisions.detail: Council passed a by-law setting 2023 fees and charges for Township services and repealing by-law 2021-62 {{vote:m1}}.
Council amended the policy, splitting arts, culture and heritage into Community Impact and Heritage categories, to be used in the 2023 budget and reviewed in the 2024 budget process {{vote:m2}}.
Council pre-approved vehicle purchases for 2023 and 2024 so staff can start procurement early given long lead times {{vote:m3}}.
Council awarded the tender to Finnbilt General Contracting Limited at $3,948,488 including contingency and excluding HST {{vote:m4}}.
Council pre-approved the replacement and awarded the tender to UrbanLink Civil Ltd. at $2,609,350 excluding contingency and HST {{vote:m5}}.
Council pre-approved the project and awarded the tender to J.G. Goetz Construction Limited at $2,393,988.98 including contingency and excluding HST {{vote:m6}}.
Council pre-approved reconstruction from St. Andrew Street to Millage Lane and authorized staff to issue a construction tender {{vote:m7}}.
Council awarded the tender to Gateman-Milloy Inc. at $4,166,000 excluding contingency and HST {{vote:m8}}.

debate: On the OLG policy, one councillor worried that dropping "arts and culture" from the category name would weaken a link to the Raceway and the agricultural society's mandate. Others asked whether pulling back economic development funding was premature, and whether 90% to Township capital was too open-ended. Staff said the capital projects are approved each year through the budget, and that Community Impact grant terms of reference would return to Council later in January.

On the East Mill Street project, staff said a south-side sidewalk is not feasible because of steep grades and homes close to the property line. A councillor asked for wayfinding signs directing pedestrians to the north-side sidewalk, and for electric charging stations to be considered. Staff said no charging stations are planned in the right-of-way.

On the 24-WG bridge, councillors asked about correspondence from residents saying it was not needed. Staff said it ranks very high on the asset management risk score and affects emergency response times. Staff also said the earlier tender was cancelled because it drew one over-budget bid, and the fall re-tender drew many more. A councillor asked about farm equipment access, and staff said the new two-lane bridge meets current design standards.

On the Elora Community Centre, councillors welcomed bids coming in well below the earlier estimate. One councillor asked that the unneeded part of the budget increase go into a reserve for future recreation needs rather than back into general capital. Staff suggested a general capital reserve for now, with the discussion to continue during strategic planning.

On parking, councillors and staff discussed delaying the long-term parking study request until after strategic planning so it can connect to active transportation. They also discussed ensuring that a 2023 interim strategy considers residents affected by parking pressures.
